chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when he fasted, if he could not find sweet food, would break his fast with water.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) use to break his fast when sweet food was not available?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) adherence to simplicity and moderation, demonstrating that the Sunnah of breaking fast is fulfilled even with the most basic sustenance like water when delicacies are unavailable. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the ease of worship, showing that the ritual act of iftar is not contingent upon luxury but on the intention and the act itself. This practice serves as a practical model for believers to maintain spiritual discipline without falling into extravagance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, when he<sup>saww</sup> was Fasting, so if he<sup>saww</sup> could not find the sweet, would break Fast upon the water’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Nawfafiy, from af-Sakuniy from Ja’far, from his father, recipients of divine supreme covenant, who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, would just have water for breakfast after sunset if Halwa (a special form of sweet) was not available.”
